findings.summary: A Gradient-Explorer-only store lives in palette/, and the 14 harnesses that reach it hardcode its path as a URL string — so the obvious tidy-up is far more expensive than it looks.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: palette/store/fullscreenStore.ts has zero consumers under palette/. Its production importers are five files in gradient-explorer/ (GradientExplorerApp, FullscreenGradientOverlay, GeometryHandleLayer, modes/fractalMode, modes/splineMode) plus gradient-explorer/gradientTargets.ts, and 14 debug/*.mts harnesses. EVIDENCE: grep -rn fullscreenStore across the tree; every debug hit is the literal string '/palette/store/fullscreenStore.ts' inside a page.evaluate dynamic import. OPTIONS: (a) move it to gradient-explorer/fullscreen/ where its consumers are — clean on paper, but it silently breaks 14 harnesses INCLUDING all three GX smokes, and nothing in tsc or knip would flag it because the references are untyped strings inside browser callbacks; (b) leave it and rely on the @invariant just added to the file, which names smoke:gx-handles and states the rename hazard explicitly; (c) move it AND sweep the 14 harnesses in the same commit, running all three GX smokes afterwards (smoke:gx-fractal-glitch needs a quiet tree and ~8 min, and smoke:liquify is ~23% flaky per cycle 11, so 'afterwards' means several runs). RECOMMENDATION: (b) for now — the annotation converts an invisible trap into a greppable one at zero risk, and the physical move buys tidiness rather than correctness. If it is ever done, do it as (c) in ONE commit, never as a rename-and-fix-callers-later. Not applied: a file move plus edits to 14 harnesses is well past what an unattended auditor should do to the load-bearing test seam of an app it is not auditing.

findings.summary: 23 of this slice's 24 files have no node-side guard at all; the 16-link test:palette chain reaches exactly one of them.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: mapping every debug/*.mts import against the 24 files gives exactly one edge — test-palette-generator.mts -> palette/features/paletteGenerator.ts. Everything else is covered only by browser boot (smoke:boot exercises registerPaletteUI, installFavients, favientsPanelPersist, paletteFiltersPersist, favientsStore.seedPresets and all four feature registrations, but only to the extent that a THROW would surface as a pageerror) or, for fullscreenStore, by the three GX smokes. Nothing asserts behaviour for favientsStore (dedupe signature, group model, import/export round-trip), generatorStore (sliceToColorBox, slot snapshot/restore), the three document bridges (untrusted-scene coercion), heroSelection, heroPrefs, pickerStore, imageStore, dragVisual or coerceJson. EVIDENCE: the per-file import map is in this audit's transcript; test:palette's 16 links are all pure-core (stopfit, stopops, channelcurve, facets, facetname, easings, generator, img2grad x2, selection, walllayout, dnd-kernels, importformats, rampgeometry, editorstore, liquify-mesh). Note debug/test-palette-editorstore.mts is NAMED for paletteEditorStore but imports palette/core/editorConfig — honest in its header, misleading from the filename, and it means a reader grepping for that store's coverage finds a file that cannot fail on it. OPTIONS: (a) add node harnesses for the three highest-risk pure-ish seams — favientsStore's isWellFormedFavient/favientSig/importCollection (it already guards against a malformed favourite bricking the shelf across sessions, and that defence is untested), the three document-bridge restore paths (they parse UNTRUSTED scene files), and heroSelection's payload-staleness assumption; (b) rename test-palette-editorstore.mts to test-palette-editorconfig.mts so the name matches what it tests; (c) accept boot-only coverage. RECOMMENDATION: (a), favientsStore first — it is the only store here that ingests untrusted input AND persists it, so a bad entry survives reloads, and its own JSDoc says exactly that. (b) is a one-line package.json + git mv but is a rename in the guard layer, which this run should not do unattended. Not applied: writing new harnesses is unreviewed code, which is Tier B by definition.

findings.summary: A rule correctly cites palette/store/favientsPanelPersist.ts in its prose but cannot load when you open that file, because its paths: front-matter has no palette entry.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: mobile-layout.md lists palette/store/favientsPanelPersist.ts as one of the eight inline re-implementations of the 768px / (pointer: coarse) test — and that citation is ACCURATE (restoreFavientsPanel does window.matchMedia?.('(pointer: coarse)').matches || window.innerWidth < 768). But its paths: block is five engine/hooks files only, so opening favientsPanelPersist.ts never loads the rule that knows about it. The pointer is one-directional. EVIDENCE: sed the front-matter of .claude/rules/mobile-layout.md; grep -rn palette .claude/rules/ returns only mobile-layout.md and sibling-apps.md. Note check:rule-guards cannot see this class — it checks whether a cited GUARD reaches a rule's paths, not whether a file a rule DISCUSSES is in its paths. OPTIONS: (a) add palette/store/favientsPanelPersist.ts to mobile-layout.md's paths:; (b) cover it from the palette rule that does not exist yet (see notes); (c) leave it. RECOMMENDATION: (b) when the palette rule is written, cross-referencing mobile-layout.md — (a) would pull a whole mobile rule into every palette-persistence edit for one line. Not applied: editing another subsystem's rule paths and creating palette rules were both explicitly out of remit, and all three palette auditors would have collided on a new rule file this cycle.

(4) smoke:boot was uncited anywhere in the palette tree. It boots index.html -> /app-gmt/main.tsx and therefore covers registerPaletteUI + installFavients + both persisters + favientsStore.seedPresets + all four feature registrations, to throw-depth. It is the single most useful guard citation for this slice after the GX smokes and should be the first line of any palette rule's Guards block.

PROPOSED CONTENTS FOR A palette.md RULE — store/feature layer only (NOT created; all three palette auditors would have collided on the file this cycle).
  paths: palette/store/**, palette/features/**, palette/registerPaletteUI.ts, palette/installFavients.ts (plus whatever p01a/p01b propose for core/ and components/).
  Read first: palette/registerPaletteUI.ts (the single registration seam — what gets registered, in what order, and why it must run before createEngineStore) and palette/installFavients.ts (the per-host mount + storageKey contract).
  Guards: `npm run smoke:boot` — the only runtime coverage of the registration path, falsified 2026-07-29 with a planted throw in mountFavientsPanel; `npx tsx debug/test-palette-generator.mts` — the only test:palette link that reaches this layer, and it pins palette/features/paletteGenerator.ts's cb* param keys against generatorStore.sliceToColorBox; `npm run smoke:gx-handles` — required for ANY change to palette/store/fullscreenStore.ts, and restart the dev server first. Do NOT cite `npm run test:palette` as a whole: check:rule-guards resolves a chained npm script by its FIRST command only, so citing it produces a false issue naming debug/test-palette-stopfit.mts (cycle 11 proved this and had to self-correct).
  Watch out: (a) fullscreenStore.ts lives here but belongs to gradient-explorer — five exports are named by string in three browser smokes, tsc cannot see the edge, do not rename or move casually; (b) the Favients COLLECTION is shared across apps (gmt.favients) while the PANEL window state is split per host by storageKey — a new host without its own key silently inherits app-gmt's; (c) mounting before applyPanelManifest fails silently, no guard catches it; (d) favientsPanelPersist.ts is one of the eight inline re-implementations of the 768px mobile test — cross-reference .claude/rules/mobile-layout.md, which names it but does not scope it; (e) DDFS discipline in this tree is currently clean, keep it that way — see below.

The four features (paletteGenerator, paletteFilters, paletteImage, paletteEditor) declare no cross-feature reads and need no dependsOn: grep for dependsOn across palette/ returns nothing, and grep for engine-slice property access shows each store touching ONLY its own feature's slice — generatorStore -> .paletteGenerator (4 sites), imageStore -> .paletteImage (2), paletteFiltersPersist -> .paletteFilters (2). No latent undeclared-access violation. dynamicVisible predicates (isMixed, isDistill, isTone, notTrace) read their own slice only. Cross-store coupling exists but is between plain zustand stores (generatorStore imports usePaletteEditorStore), which the isolation rule does not govern.
